note: Mussel / clam / scallop / oyster / periwinkle at true size, catch pass 2. Item and handful cells, palettes and the tiny-kind pixel patterns read from Shellfish2; bed and flat contracts measured by calling it.

camera.view: top-down 3/4 read (y x 0.64 = sin 40 deg), same upper-left key

item.pivotIs: ground contact — the odd loose shell on a deck

handful.pivotIs: THE GRIP — one clutch per hand, pin to a CharacterIso hand anchor

scale.rule: strict world scale: 32 px = 1 m, so a mussel is 2x1 px, a clam 2x2, a scallop or oyster 3x3, a periwinkle one pixel. Nothing is inflated to read alone — the beds carry it.

tiny.note: the 1-2 px kinds are explicit pixel patterns, one per variant: [dx, dy, rampIndex] from the placement pixel

bed.call: bed(kind, {w, h, seed, cover}) -> {w, h, rgba}
bed.use: alpha-masked texture laid over rock / sand / mud: mussels + periwinkles on tide-pool rock, oyster clumps on the mud edge, scallops apart on sand. A clam flat shows NO clams — see flat.

densityPerPx._transcribed: internal `dens` table in bed(); coverage blobs (2 + 3 x cover of them) leave ground showing between

flat.holes: holes(seed, n, w, h) -> [{x, y, phase, period, dur}] — the keyholes a clam flat shows
flat.spurt: spurt(hole, tMs) -> null | {rise 0..1, u 0..1}; rise = sin(pi x u) over dur. Draw a 1 px jet, rise x 4 px tall; a droplet 1 px above it once u > 0.45. This is the gameplay TELL for the dig.

heap.call: heap(kind, w, h, seed, mask(x,y), {dome(x,y)}) -> rgba
heap.use: heaped shells clipped to a container opening — THE container fill for shellfish at this scale; CatchKit2.heap wraps it for a rim polygon

layering.rule: held rests (and anything pinned to a hand anchor) draw UNDER the character sprite for NW / N / NE, over it otherwise
